liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Other One** (3 reviews): Ranked among the year's best Other Ones, with a great extended jam after the second verse; The Other One builds out of Space, with Phil and Jerry especially fierce [25][29][32]
- **Uncle John's Band** (2 reviews): Uncle John's Band dissolving into a Playin' jam and then space is well above average, with standout keyboard sounds; Uncle John's Band, as it started up, was some of the most fluid Dead playing [24][32]
- **Box of Rain** (1 review): Box of Rain closed the first set [33]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): The China Cat, Rider, Playin', Uncle John's sequence is rated top shelf [24]
- **I Know You Rider** (1 review): Energy surges right after the line about a north bound train [28]
- **Wharf Rat** (1 review): Reviewer ranks this Wharf Rat among the best ever played [30]

## Setlist highlights

- **set break Stealy**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [35]
- **NFA chant - tuning**: rare: 3 archived performances [35]

## The recordings

- **gd1989-08-19.139669.mtx.photoLeon.LL.t-flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 162 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1989-08-19.mtx.hansokolow.96303.sbeok.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 156 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [2]
- **gd89-08-19.sbd.5213.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 151 min; rated 4.53/5 by 19 [7]. Said about its sound: Soundboard sounds like a Healy mix, with excellent clarity, sound field and balance; Reviewer says the sound quality on this matrix is top notch [24][33]
- **gd1989-08-19.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.83775.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 151 min; rated 3.33/5 by 12 [9]
- **gd1989-08-19.164141.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac1644**: soundboard; 19 songs; 153 min [11]

## Around the show

- Reviewer loved the venue's stone construction and its thrones [26]
- Reviewer describes it as the last Greek Theatre show and a fitting end [29]
- The crowd chanted for Phil during the first set [33]
- This was the band's 29th and final performance at the Greek Theatre in Berkeley [40]
- Reviewer calls it the best of the three-night Greek run, and the band's last show at that venue [23]
- Reviewer recalls a Jerry interview before the Hampton shows naming this show and 10-1-89 as the band's best recently [25]
- No bust-outs in this show, but it still rocked [26]
- Reviewer saw 191 shows from 1985 to 1995 and puts this in their top three [32]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1989-08-19.139669.mtx.photoLeon.LL.t-flac16**: transferred by Three Source Matrix created in Audacity by photoLeon; source: Three Source Matrix created in Audacity [1]
- **gd1989-08-19.mtx.hansokolow.96303.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by hansokolow; source: Matrix mix (SBD/AUD) [2]. Also: Matrix made by hansokolow in ProTools from soundboard cassette masters, with transfers and mastering by Charlie Miller; Cassette masters were played on a Tascam 122mkII into an Apogee MiniMe at 24bit/48k; Two soundboard cassette masters were combined to make the show seamless; tapes came from Paul Scotton and Joani Walker [2]
- **gd89-08-19.sbd.5213.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD Cassette Master > DAT > .WAV > .SHN [7]. Also: A strong FM broadcast of the show led to high-quality recordings circulating widely [23]
- **gd1989-08-19.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.83775.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG90) D [9]. Also: Two soundboard cassette masters were used for a seamless show; tapes supplied by Paul Scotton and Joani Walker [9]
- **gd1989-08-19.164141.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac1644**: taped by Set 1 recorded by Joani Walker -- Set 2 recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  February 11, 2023; source: Ultramatrix SBD > Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/Maxell MX90/TDK MA-XG90) [11]. Also: Set 1 was recorded by Joani Walker, with masters supplied by Paul Scotton; Multiple ultramatrix masters were combined to make the show complete [11]

claims.text: Reviewer calls it the best of the three-night Greek run, and the band's last show at that venue
A strong FM broadcast of the show led to high-quality recordings circulating widely
Soundboard sounds like a Healy mix, with excellent clarity, sound field and balance
The China Cat, Rider, Playin', Uncle John's sequence is rated top shelf
Uncle John's Band dissolving into a Playin' jam and then space is well above average, with standout keyboard sounds
Ranked among the year's best Other Ones, with a great extended jam after the second verse
Reviewer recalls a Jerry interview before the Hampton shows naming this show and 10-1-89 as the band's best recently
Reviewer loved the venue's stone construction and its thrones
No bust-outs in this show, but it still rocked
Energy surges right after the line about a north bound train
Reviewer describes it as the last Greek Theatre show and a fitting end
The Other One builds out of Space, with Phil and Jerry especially fierce
Real fireworks come after the last lyrics, with tension building and holding repeatedly
Reviewer ranks this Wharf Rat among the best ever played
Reviewer saw 191 shows from 1985 to 1995 and puts this in their top three
The Other One out of Space is the best single-song performance the reviewer ever witnessed
Uncle John's Band, as it started up, was some of the most fluid Dead playing
The crowd chanted for Phil during the first set
Box of Rain closed the first set
Reviewer says the sound quality on this matrix is top notch
Matrix made by hansokolow in ProTools from soundboard cassette masters, with transfers and mastering by Charlie Miller
Cassette masters were played on a Tascam 122mkII into an Apogee MiniMe at 24bit/48k
Two soundboard cassette masters were combined to make the show seamless; tapes came from Paul Scotton and Joani Walker
Two soundboard cassette masters were used for a seamless show; tapes supplied by Paul Scotton and Joani Walker
Set 1 was recorded by Joani Walker, with masters supplied by Paul Scotton
Set 2 was recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy
Multiple ultramatrix masters were combined to make the show complete
